title: Keep the release-notes feed valid whatever the titles say

blocks.text: The changelog page publishes a feed of release notes, one XML `<entry>` per release, built from a text block in `FeedEntry`. Release managers type the titles and their own names. Since the note "Fixes for Q&A and R&D" went out, feed readers show an error instead of the feed, and a title that mentioned an HTML tag came out as something else.

Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/FeedEntry.java`: `escape(text)` returns the text so that an XML parser reads it back exactly as typed, inside an element and inside an attribute value written in double quotes.
About four lines. The tests parse every entry with the JDK's own XML parser.

cases.says: an entry with plain values keeps the template's layout and parses back to the same title, author and link
a title with & in it still parses, and reads back unchanged
a title that contains markup and an entity name reads back as the same text, not as markup and not escaped twice
an author name with double quotes in it reads back unchanged from the attribute

origin.section: HTML and XML Keep Their Quotes in a Text Block, and Every Inserted Value Still Needs Escaping

concepts: Values formatted into an HTML or XML text block are escaped first, & before the rest and quotes inside attributes, or they break the document or become markup.
